title: Reflections and Rotations with Coordinates Practice
description: Practice applying coordinate rules for reflections and common rotations.

questions.question: Which rule represents a reflection across the x-axis?
questions.explanation: A reflection across the x-axis keeps x the same and changes the sign of y.

questions.question: Reflect point A(6, -2) across the y-axis. What is A'?
questions.explanation: Across the y-axis, x changes sign and y stays the same: (6, -2) -> (-6, -2).

questions.question: Reflect point B(-4, 9) across the origin. What is B'?
questions.explanation: Across the origin, both coordinates change signs: (-4, 9) -> (4, -9).

questions.question: Reflect point C(8, -3) across the line y = x. What is C'?
questions.explanation: Across y = x, the coordinates switch places: (8, -3) -> (-3, 8).

questions.question: Which rule represents a 90° counterclockwise rotation about the origin?
questions.explanation: A 90° counterclockwise rotation about the origin uses (x, y) -> (-y, x).

questions.question: Rotate point D(5, 7) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What is D'?
Rotate point E(-2, 6) 180° about the origin. What is E'?
Rotate point F(-3, -8) 270° counterclockwise about the origin. What is F'?
questions.explanation: Use (x, y) -> (y, -x): (-3, -8) -> (-8, 3). Wait carefully: -x = 3, so the correct image is (-8, 3).

questions.question: A reflection and a rotation can change the position of a figure without changing its size or shape.
questions.explanation: Reflections and rotations are rigid transformations, so they preserve size and shape.

questions.question: Complete the image point: Reflect G(10, -4) across the x-axis to get G' = ____.
questions.explanation: Across the x-axis, x stays the same and y changes sign, so (10, -4) becomes (10, 4).
